_comment: The first coverage of vendored-remote-resources, which could not be reached until the network could be faked: its lane needs a VERIFIED vendor result, and the harness could only make a fetch fail. lib/theme.css matches the bytes its declared source serves and the package is popular, so the file is that release's - and the remote @import on its first line is the release's own line, not something the developer wrote. So remote-resources does NOT report it as a finding; vendored-remote-resources puts it to a person instead, who decides whether shipping the release as published is acceptable. The locus carries the release it was matched against as its hint. Escalations are not expressible in `expect`, so the golden holds it.
